Get the data or the argset of one analysis at the console

Source: R/console.R
get_data.Rd

get_data() returns the data that the analyses of one scenario and simulation of the plan p get as data. get_argset() returns the argset of one analysis, so you do not type the name of the analysis.

Usage

get_data(p, scenario = "real", sim = 1)

get_argset(p, scenario = "real", sim = 1, name, i = 1)

Arguments

p

A plan from plnr::Plan$new(), with data from add_data(). get_argset() also needs analyses from add_analyses().

scenario

The scenario. The default is "real".

sim

The simulation, a whole number from 1 to the number of simulations of the scenario.

name

The name of the analysis kind, for example "models".

i

The counter of the extra dimensions of the kind, see add_analyses(). A kind without extra dimensions has 1 only.

Value

get_data(): a named list with one element for each data element, and hash. get_argset(): the argset, a named list.

Details

get_data(p, "null", 3) calls p$get_data() for the analysis null__sim_0003__pbn_n_rows. add_analyses() adds this analysis for each scenario and simulation, and it gets the same data as each other analysis of that scenario and simulation. So get_data() takes the path of p$get_data(): the seed sim, the steps of add_data(), and the cache with its one line. The value is the named list of the data elements, with the element hash that plnr adds. pbn::get_data(p)$d is the data d of "real".

get_argset(p, "null", 3, "models", 2) is p$get_argset("null__sim_0003__models__2").

Call get_argset() after add_analyses(). Call get_data() after add_data(), before or after run_plan(). Before add_analyses(), get_data() takes the scenarios of the last call of scenarios() before add_data(). initialize_project() forgets them. It then calls each data function with the scenario, the simulation and the settings, in the same way as plnr. The value then has no element hash. So the line d <- pbn::get_data(p, "real")$d works directly after add_data() in a run script.

Both stop on a scenario or a simulation that the plan does not hold, and the error names the values that it holds. get_argset() also stops on a kind or a counter that the plan does not hold for that scenario. An example is a kind with control = TRUE for "real".

To step through an action function by hand, put these lines first in it:

if (plnr::is_run_directly()) {
  argset <- pbn::get_argset(p, "null", 3, "models")
  data <- pbn::get_data(p, "null", 3)
}

See also

vignette("pbn"), which steps through one analysis by hand.

Other plan: add_analyses(), add_data(), cohort_data(), progress(), run_plan()

Examples

CFG <- list(scenarios = data.frame(scenario = c("real", "null"), sims = 2))
p <- plnr::Plan$new()
pbn::add_data(p, "d", fn = function(scenario, sim) {
  return(data.frame(x = stats::rnorm(3)))
})
pbn::add_analyses(
  p,
  pbn::scenarios(CFG),
  name = "means",
  fn = function(data, argset) return(data.frame(mean = mean(data$d$x))),
  outcome = c("y1", "y2")
)
pbn::get_data(p, "null", 2)$d
#>            x
#> 1 -0.8969145
#> 2  0.1848492
#> 3  1.5878453
pbn::get_argset(p, "null", 2, "means", 2)$outcome
#> [1] "y2"
